0.comment: Candace: Aaru Village and the Guardian
0.content:
Aaru Village lies in the Land of Lower Setekh, beside a mountain and a lake at the edge of the Great Red Sand. Its people call it the last refuge of King Deshret's descendants, a title shared by every Guardian. The Guardian enforces a simple code: anyone who keeps the rules may rest and receive help; those who break it become the village's "enemies". Repentant offenders get supplies and banishment; the rest "find company only with the desert sands". Candace was appointed at eight with the charge of guarding the villagers until the last of them faded away in peace.

The village grew from survivors of King Deshret's city, Akhtamun. The Akademiya later used it as a place of exile for scholars driven mad (the Village Keepers). Under Candace and village head Uncle Anpu it opened to trade. Merchants, researchers, Dehya's mercenaries and investigation teams now pass through. It also brought fake merchants, caravan hijackers and an exodus of young people.

By 2026 several village children had been accepted into the Akademiya. Candace calls this the finest birthday gift she could ask for, because the children of Aaru can now freely choose their futures. In 6.6 the village received the evacuated population of the rainforest.

1.content:
Every new Guardian is told, on taking up the shield, that the Guardians have never been blessed by any god. The news broke some predecessors: they gave up training, or decided that unwatched meant unbound and turned lawless. Candace was not discouraged: her lance and shield are not a prayer for blessing, and her duty does not change whether a god favours her or not. Outsiders still believe she carries Al-Ahmar's blessing, and she keeps the secret.

The irony is that her Vision, the mark of the gods' approval, came at the moment she broke with tradition. It appeared on her lance after she told the old Guardians that if they could not move forward, she would protect the village's future herself.

2.content:
Dehya of the Eremites is Candace's closest friend and opposite: loud where she is calm, reckless where she is careful. Dehya keeps her mercenaries on their best behaviour in Aaru Village, which Candace appreciates, and Candace calls her "really quite adorable" underneath. Dehya gives her jewellery and clothes, begs her to take time off and threatens to guard the village herself so Candace can go shopping.

In 3.1 Candace bluntly warned Dehya not to start another fight under her roof, then welcomed her back. They travelled together to the Akademiya Extravaganza (3.6, limited event), where Dehya tried to buy her outfits and a makeup box. In the 6.1 Fieldwise event (limited) they ran the Security Division's combat tests together, and Candace reminded Dehya to settle the Traveler's pay. She also passed Dehya's gift of fine clothes to the Blazing Beasts' accountant, who had a use for them.

The two coordinate between desert and rainforest peoples; in the 6.1 event Candace said the Blazing Beasts would be staying in Aaru Village for the foreseeable future. Before the 6.6 battle, Dehya wanted a drink and Candace suggested prayer. In 7.1 they keep watch together near Mt. Damavand, where Dehya's crew has made camp, on the Nail of Retribution.

3.content:
Candace met the General Mahamatra in 3.1 when he and Alhaitham clashed outside her village; she made them talk out their quarrel under the village head's roof. She later decided he was "more compassionate than I gave you credit for" when he agreed to let young Isak help look for his grandfather. She notes that the Eremites tell terrifying stories about him and that he now visits the desert often.

In 4.7 she and Dehya met Cyno at Caravan Ribat as he hunted for his missing professor. Candace told him to pack for five extra days and offered help without asking about the confidential case. In the 5.1 event (limited) she said she rarely gets to see him outside work. In 6.6 Cyno said her interrogation skills had improved a lot in recent years, and she fought beside him in the assault on Fatui-held Sumeru City.

4.comment: Candace: Uncle Anpu and the opening of the village
4.content:
Uncle Anpu, the village head, decided Aaru Village had to change for its people's future and invited a cloth caravan from Sumeru City. The retired Guardians called it betrayal and demanded Candace drive the merchants out. She refused, ended the argument with a clang of lance on shield, and told the elders to rest. Then she escorted the caravan in and out herself. Word of profitable trade with Aaru spread among Sumeru's merchants.

When the influx brought crime and emigration, the old Guardians challenged her again. Her furious answer, and the Vision that followed, settled the matter. In 3.1 Anpu shared his suspicion that the abductor of the Village Keepers had Akademiya links. He also once refused the Akademiya's request to take the Keepers back.

5.content:
Candace met the Traveler in 3.1 and named them an honoured guest of Aaru Village for life. She asks them for stories of faraway lands, tells them desert legends by the fire, and keeps watch so they can sleep. In her birthday letters she credits the growing bonds between the village and the rainforest to the Traveler's deeds and promises protection and restful nights whenever they visit.

Before Jnagarbha Day (3.2) she made the Traveler promise not to be reckless and prayed for their success. In the limited 5.1 event they investigated the mysterious gem together, and in 6.1 she offered to tailor them a sand-proof cloak so all would know they were the village's guest. Paimon once described her as being like a nice older sister.

6.comment: Candace: The Village Keepers and Isak
6.content:
In the 3.1 Archon Quest the Village Keepers, exiled scholars living in Aaru Village, began vanishing. Candace told the Traveler and Cyno about Isak, a boy raised by village families after his grandfather died. He had adopted an elderly mad scholar as his "grandpa" after the man once calmly taught him the names of the stars. Desert radicals captured by Dehya and the Traveler told Candace, under interrogation, that a masked "envoy of King Deshret" had given them incense to lure the Keepers away. She stayed behind to guard the radicals while the others pursued the trail, which led to the corrupt sages' plot.

She observed of the desert that nearly everyone there carries hardship or regret, and that this is exactly why she fights. Before the 3.2 Jnagarbha Day operation, the plotters met in the village chief's home. She stayed to protect the village and prayed for them.

7.content:
Nefer came to Aaru Village as a child after her tribe was destroyed. Candace was one of the few children willing to talk to her; together they drove off wild beasts and bandits and cared for people in hardship. When Nefer was about to leave for the Akademiya, Candace held her hands and told her to write. Nefer's letters described the Darshans and the Grand Bazaar. A draft she never sent confessed the prejudice she faced and that she missed Candace.

By 6.6 Nefer was back in the desert. Nefer had told Candace about Dori's quiet charity, to Dori's annoyance; Dehya explained that Nefer and Candace "go way back" and close friends share such things. Candace said it was Nefer's way of showing she cares. Naphis put Dehya, Candace and Nefer in charge of negotiating between the various parties in the 6.6 crisis.

8.content: The first time Layla woke from sleepwalking, she found herself in Aaru Village with all her essays done, and a heterochromatic stranger looking after her. Candace saw she looked unwell and fed her; Layla talked about astrology and the stars, which Candace only half followed but found enchanting. Layla thought the stars had sent a messenger. At the 3.6 Extravaganza (limited event) they met again; Candace greeted her by name and caught the Swiftfly Layla had been chasing. Layla's own voice-over shows she only later learned her rescuer was called Candace.

9.comment: Candace: Sethos and the Temple of Silence
9.content:
Sethos, the young leader of the hidden Temple of Silence, recommends Candace's hospitality: portions even he could barely finish. He adds that it is best to receive her hospitality rather than her wrath. She has heard of Hermanubis's power in a "worthy vessel" and looks forward to hosting him. In the 6.6 aftermath they parted at Caravan Ribat, promising to stop by the Temple, which the Goat King and Ibis King were about to visit.

In the limited 5.1 event each of them unknowingly bought half of the same split gem, the Wedjat Eye. Sethos traced it to the first Sabzeruz Festival and proposed that the Temple keep both halves; Candace agreed.

10.content:
Candace is grateful that the Dendro Archon's benevolence lets desertfolk like her live in peace, but she remains first a child of the desert. She took part in the plan that freed Nahida in 3.2 by guarding Aaru Village. In 6.6 she said that belief and friendship are both choices, pointing to Dunyarzad's friendship with the Archon. In 7.1 she said the desertfolk ought not leave the Dendro Archon to carry the burden alone.

In the limited 5.1 event she helped plan a Sabzeruz birthday surprise for Nahida. She chose not to hand the Wedjat Eye back to her, fearing its broken memories held only grief.

key: Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana
11.content:
When Irminsul began failing and Nahida collapsed, the rainforest's people were evacuated to Caravan Ribat and then to Aaru Village, where Candace received them. The cause proved to be Dottore, working from within Irminsul. On the day of the counter-operation, Candace's unit (with Cyno, Dehya, Tighnari, the Wanderer, Jeht, Rahman, Rana and the Traveler) fought into Fatui-held Sumeru City. Pantalone, acting as a decoy, stalled them for Dottore. Before the battle she prayed for her companions' safe return.

Moved across the battlefield by the Seven Pillars' chessboard, she marvelled at their power and helped secure the harbour. Afterwards she and Dehya escorted every evacuee home. She prayed never to have to leave again, hoping to stay "in this peaceful paradise of our own choosing", and returned to Aaru Village to distribute supplies.

key: Chromatic Ode of Candies and Roses
12.content: During the limited-time 5.1 Sabzeruz event, Candace bought a gem with strange elemental energy and began seeing events seconds before they happened. She saved a child from a falling crate and warned a vendor about his stove. Investigating with the Traveler, she traced the gem through Dori to a desert ruin. A mysterious caravan "robbery" in the desert turned out to be the Pari Sorush punishing a suspicious caravan, and the twin gem had been bought by Sethos. Her visions shifted to fragments of the past. Sethos revealed that the gem was the Wedjat Eye: by legend, King Deshret's gift to "Lesser Lord Kusanali" (whom the Traveler understands to have been Rukkhadevata) at the first Sabzeruz, which resonates only with the people of Al-Ahmar. The halves went to the Temple of Silence. Afterwards she played tanbur for Nilou's dance in the parade.

13.content: The Akademiya invited Candace and Dehya to its Extravaganza, and the villagers pushed her to go. In the city she wandered happily and bought gifts for the village. She refused a makeup box, and when Nilou picked out clothes she wished they were sturdier. With Dehya she overheard hired thugs targeting a man named Sachin and warned the Traveler, noting that the two of them had less freedom to act inside the city. Asked what she would do with a fortune, she said food and water sources.

14.comment: Candace: Windblume's Breath and Setaria (3.5 event)
14.content: During the limited-time 3.5 Windblume event, Candace stood in as bodyguard for Setaria, an educator working in Aaru Village, while Rahman was busy with the Eremites. It was her first bodyguard job, a taste of Dehya's line of work. She agreed with Cyno that teachers willing to work in the desert need protection.

15.comment: Candace: Fieldwise Center Security Division (6.1 event)
15.content: In a limited-time 6.1 event the Akademiya's new Fieldwise Center required every investigation team entering dangerous areas to include at least two members who had passed a combat assessment. Candace and Dehya ran the tests with Blazing Beasts mercenaries and put the proceeds toward repairing Aaru Village facilities. She hosted a feast for Faruzan, Amber, Collei and the Traveler. She offered to sew sand-proof cloaks for the Blazing Beasts and approved of updating traditional desert food within reason, since nothing must go to waste.

16.content: Candace buys information from Dori and gave her a travel permit and tax waiver in exchange for help in the 5.1 event (limited). In 6.6 Dori gave her and Dehya free supplies because they had rescued a caravan carrying her goods. Candace publicly thanked her for funding desert shelters for children and the elderly, which Dori had hoped to keep quiet.

17.comment: Candace: King Deshret and the desert faith
17.content: Candace tells the legend of King Deshret, "Ahmar" to the desertfolk: king of warriors, gardeners and scholars, whose folly buried his city. She believes most desertfolk cling to the hope of his resurrection and that it cannot happen. Her shield is said to bear the blessing of Bennu, one of his Seven Pillars; in 6.6 she saw the Pillars' power first-hand, and Bennu spoke through her shield. She speaks of night as a goddess and prays to "the gods" without naming one.

18.content: After the 7.1 Archon Quest, Celestial Nails across Teyvat began acting strangely. Candace and Dehya went to Tanit Camps to watch the one at Mt. Damavand, where Dehya's crew set up camp. Dehya's mercenaries treated it as sightseeing; Candace insisted it was an investigation, or at least observation. She said the desertfolk ought not leave the Dendro Archon to carry the burden alone. When Dehya remarked that Sumeru is now better prepared for a crisis, Candace answered that this is because everyone has learned to stand together.
